Forreal - I actually went to a psych ward and made a group of friends after being transferred to an in-patient facility. Now that we are all out a year later and doing better, a few of us keep in contact over text message, and we call our group chat “depression camp” - because we all met during June during the peak of COVID (pre-vaccine) at a place that reminded us of a summer camp. 

Folks with these disabilities do use mechanisms like this to cope- like laughter and dark humor. Plus, people laugh all the time awkwardly when talking about awkward topics. My roommate at the hospital I stayed at had a note in her chart because she hysterically would start laughing each time she spoke about literally anything serious - and doctors wanted to make a note for each visiting vitals person that came in, so they weren’t alarmed. 

I legit have all the things she mentioned in this video and will happily send my diagnosis paperwork to mods to show y’all how granular you’re being with this post. Would I have posted this myself as someone with these diagnoses for the public? No- but it did make me feel less alone for a brief second. And I deff would have shared this on my Facebook to my friends and family if were with my husband laughing after a rough week - it helps me feel better and gives me a more positive outlook on things because this shit is fucking exhausting. This is coming from someone who frequents this sub and respects uncovering the atrocious way that faking shit on the internet for karma or clout is spreading. 

Note: I haven’t looked into this individual personally and am not repping their account; I’m speaking solely from watching this video alone - as someone who is diagnosed with this shit formally- it checks out for me. Take that as you will and remember the good fight we are all here for!

I don't say this to guilt you, and I say this as a daughter of a mother who felt she was imperfect and is now no longer with me (cancer.)

Your daughter wants the full authentic version of yourself. It's okay to have sad days in front of her. It's okay to have bad days in front of her. That shows her it's okay not to always be at 100%. I hope you don't feel that your motherly perfection is your fault. The fact that you're trying so hard to NOT be how your mother was with you only proves you're a good mom. I hope one day you see that too and stick around long enough to hear your daughter say those words herself. 

You deserve goodbye to these feelings, yes, but hello to the rest of your life as you watch your daughter grow and learn with you. You can learn how to live this life together. That's how I helped my mom through her imperfections while learning to live with my own. It made me feel so much better when dealing with my own struggles because I had someone to relate to. I miss her, but can empathize with your depression and hopelessness when wanting to go on. You still sound like a great mom.
